QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Process and Governance_47

question.text: Ms. Kavita Reddy, an external IC member of 'Aravalli Category II AIF', realises that a company being evaluated is a supplier to a business she personally chairs. Under the IC Code of Conduct, her CORRECT course is:

answer.text: Resign from the IC immediately and permanently
Vote in favour of the investment to cement the supplier relationship
Disclose the conflict in a timely manner to the Manager, adhere to AIF policies, and recuse herself from this decision
Proceed to vote normally; it's a small supplier relationship

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI's Code of Conduct for IC members requires timely disclosure of the conflict to the Manager, adherence to AIF conflict-policy, and — where necessary — recusal from the specific decision. Resignation is disproportionate; voting in the conflicted transaction directly violates the Code. The Trap: Proceeding and pro-investment voting both breach fiduciary duty. Resignation is a nuclear option reserved for systemic or persistent conflicts. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the disclose-adhere-recuse sequence. Same principle in III-A/C, XXI-B, X-A/X-B. Manager's Pro-Tip: Codify recusal in the IC charter: (i) disclosure at agenda stage, (ii) physical absence for the discussion, (iii) abstention from the vote, (iv) minute entry noting recusal. This documentation defends against post-hoc allegations.
